'''Uriah Watkins''' (DeckTech handle '''travler'''; Players Committee forum handle '''Lt. Travler''')<ref name="dt-23661">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/23661 Testing Testing 1 2 3 (4 5 6)], DeckTech (Uriah "travler" Watkins, 29 May 2002). Preservation copies: [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/23661/ Stephen Skilton]; [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/23661/ GitHub Pages]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009124811/http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/23661/ Wayback Machine].</ref><ref name="pcf-3383-47783" /> posted a [[Light]] [[Mind What You Have Learned / Save You It Can|Mind What You Have Learned]] list on DeckTech (''Testing Testing 1 2 3 (4 5 6)'').

With [[Glenn Hall]] he directed the 2004 Oregon State Championship, which drew 13 players.<ref name="pcf-3383-47783">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=47783#47783 2004 Oregon State SWCCG Championship Event], Glenn Hall, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (20 June 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040716072317/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=47947%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In June 2004 he wrote that he had attended both the Washington and the Oregon State Championships in 2003.<ref name="pcf-3383-47038">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=47038#47038 2004 Oregon State SWCCG Championship Event], Uriah Watkins, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (1 June 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625210617/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=47102%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In September 2003 he described [[Classic]] as a format that leveled the playing field and put more weight on playing skill than on the choice of deck, with a less predictable metagame than [[Open]].<ref name="pcf-1063-32675">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=32675#32675 Classic / Non-Classic], Uriah Watkins, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (6 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040918135527/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=20831%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
